<a id="GNT-33.9-monotonic-and-wall-separation"></a>

**[GNT-33.9-monotonic-and-wall-separation] Monotonic and wall separation.** A deadline, timeout, or elapsed-time measurement is expressed over a monotonic instant and MUST NOT be derived from a wall clock or a civil time, and observing wall time is an explicit operation whose result is one instant value rather than ambient state. A declared deadline over a wall-clock or civil value is refused under the host-consultation-refused diagnostic.

<a id="GNT-33.10-rule-data-upgrade-and-staleness"></a>

**[GNT-33.10-rule-data-upgrade-and-staleness] Rule-data upgrade and staleness.** Rule data never changes under a pinned identity: an installed or host database update MUST NOT silently alter the semantics of a declared identity, and a value computed under a superseded identity is refused under the stale-rule-data diagnostic rather than recomputed. A deliberate upgrade declares the source identity, the target identity, and the migration, and an upgrade that would replace a pinned identity without that exact declaration is refused under the silent-rule-data-upgrade diagnostic.

<a id="GNT-33.11-durable-replay-retention"></a>

**[GNT-33.11-durable-replay-retention] Durable replay retention.** A durable record that depends on locale, calendar, or zone data retains the pinned rule-data identity, the committed observation, and the disambiguation declaration it used, so replay is a function of committed values rather than of the host's current preferences or databases. Replay MUST NOT consult the host clock, the host locale, or a newly installed database, and a record whose retained identity is unavailable is refused under the rule-data-unavailable diagnostic rather than replayed under a different identity.

<a id="GNT-33.12-locale-and-time-non-claims"></a>

**[GNT-33.12-locale-and-time-non-claims] Locale and time non-claims.** This section does not promise complete locale, calendar, or zone coverage; does not promise that any host database is correct, current, or stable; does not define a host clock, timer, or scheduler; does not make platform formatting, parsing, or collation authoritative; does not grant authority through a locale or zone value; and does not define durable runtime storage, checkpointing, or recovery mechanisms. Model facts and tests MUST NOT be presented as such guarantees.


## 34. Standard-Library Logical Package Architecture

<a id="GNT-34.0-standard-library-package-architecture"></a>

**[GNT-34.0-standard-library-package-architecture] Standard-library package architecture.** This section defines an analyzer-only declaration model for the canonical logical standard-library hierarchy, its internal dependency DAG, its edition prelude, facade identity, stability tiers, applicability, and contract versioning. Its pure model is `crates/gantry-ir/src/stdlib.rs` and its analyzer evidence is `crates/gantry-conformance/tests/stdlib_architecture.rs`. The frozen architecture diagnostics are `std-invalid-package-name` (`GNT-34.1`), `std-duplicate-package` (`GNT-34.1`), `std-invalid-name-classification` (`GNT-34.2`), `std-unknown-edge`, `std-dependency-cycle`, `std-pure-to-capability-edge`, and `std-package-to-adapter-edge` (`GNT-34.3`), `std-unenumerated-prelude-member` and `std-wildcard-prelude-refused` (`GNT-34.4`), `std-facade-identity-loss` (`GNT-34.5`), `std-invalid-stability-transition` (`GNT-34.6`), `std-unsupported-applicability` and `std-feature-mutates-instance` (`GNT-34.7`), `std-layout-derived-identity` (`GNT-34.8`), `std-contract-version-mismatch` (`GNT-34.9`), `std-invalid-relocation` (`GNT-34.10`), `std-publication-drift` (`GNT-34.11`), and `std-non-claim-as-guarantee` (`GNT-34.12`); each diagnostic names one owning clause and no spelling is shared by two refusal conditions. Physical Rust crate layout is nonsemantic: splitting or combining crates MUST NOT change logical source identity, and this section introduces no family behavior, no package downloader, no generator, and no publication mechanism.

<a id="GNT-34.1-canonical-hierarchy-and-package-names"></a>

**[GNT-34.1-canonical-hierarchy-and-package-names] Canonical hierarchy and package names.** The hierarchy is rooted at `std` and contains exactly the declared logical families: the pure families `std.core`, `std.collections`, `std.text`, `std.num`, `std.codec`, `std.crypto`, and `std.data`, and the capability-backed families `std.io`, `std.fs`, `std.net`, `std.process`, `std.env`, `std.console`, `std.time`, `std.random`, `std.observe`, `std.artifact`, `std.secret`, `std.agent`, and `std.test`. A package name is one lowercase dotted path rooted at `std` with at least two segments; a malformed or non-rooted spelling is refused under the invalid-package-name diagnostic, and a name declared twice is refused under the duplicate-package diagnostic.

<a id="GNT-34.2-name-classification"></a>

**[GNT-34.2-name-classification] Name classification.** Every declared name is exactly one of package, module, facade, generated declaration, or implementation-only intrinsic, and the classification is frozen by the declaration. A module belongs to exactly one package, a facade re-exports public items without defining them, a generated declaration is produced by the governed generator path, and an implementation-only intrinsic is not source identity. A name that declares no classification, two classifications, a package classification inside another package, or a classification its owning package does not admit is refused under the invalid-name-classification diagnostic.

<a id="GNT-34.3-acyclic-internal-dependency-dag"></a>

**[GNT-34.3-acyclic-internal-dependency-dag] Acyclic internal dependency DAG.** A dependency edge names one other declared standard package, so an edge naming an undeclared std package is refused under the unknown-edge diagnostic, a reference outside the std hierarchy is a host-adapter edge refused under the package-to-adapter diagnostic, and a dependency relation containing a cycle is refused under the dependency-cycle diagnostic, which names exactly one declared package that lies on the cycle. A pure family MUST NOT depend on a capability-backed family, refused under the pure-to-capability diagnostic, and no standard package MUST depend on a host adapter, refused under the package-to-adapter diagnostic. Every declared edge is classified, and the DAG admits one deterministic topological order that does not depend on declaration order.

<a id="GNT-34.4-edition-prelude-and-explicit-imports"></a>

**[GNT-34.4-edition-prelude-and-explicit-imports] Edition prelude and explicit imports.** The automatic prelude is one closed, edition-versioned, enumerated set of names; a member that is not enumerated is refused under the unenumerated-prelude-member diagnostic, and an implicit wildcard import is refused under the wildcard-prelude-refused diagnostic. Every other name is reached by an explicit import that names its defining package, so an import MUST NOT gain authority, identity, or a stability tier from the importing package. Adding or removing a prelude member is an edition change with exact compatibility consequences rather than a silent extension.

<a id="GNT-34.5-facade-and-reexport-identity"></a>

**[GNT-34.5-facade-and-reexport-identity] Facade and re-export identity.** A facade path and a re-export preserve the defining package's item identity: the same item read through a facade and through its defining package has one identity, one stability tier, and one interface-digest entry. A facade that would rewrite, merge, or substitute an item's defining identity, or that would expose an item its defining package does not export, is refused under the facade-identity-loss diagnostic rather than accepted as a convenience path.

<a id="GNT-34.6-stability-tiers"></a>

**[GNT-34.6-stability-tiers] Stability tiers.** Every public standard-library item declares exactly one tier: foundational, stable, target-specific, or experimental. A tier transition is an explicit, versioned, compatibility-relevant decision, and a transition that would widen stability silently, leave one item with two tiers, move an item backwards, or enter or leave the foundational tier is refused under the invalid-stability-transition diagnostic. Experimental and target-specific items are never presented as stable.

<a id="GNT-34.7-applicability-and-feature-granularity"></a>

**[GNT-34.7-applicability-and-feature-granularity] Applicability and feature granularity.** Every package declares the semantic modes and targets it is available for, and a use outside its declared applicability is refused under the unsupported-applicability diagnostic before execution rather than resolved against a host fact. A feature selection names the exact package set it enables and MUST NOT silently mutate an already selected package instance; a selection that would change an existing instance's identity, interface, or requirements is refused under the feature-mutates-instance diagnostic.

<a id="GNT-34.8-defining-identity-and-interface-digest"></a>

**[GNT-34.8-defining-identity-and-interface-digest] Defining identity and interface digest.** Every public `std` item has exactly one defining logical package and one stable identity, and each package publishes one interface digest over its exported items, their classes, stability tiers, and applicability. Physical repository layout, Rust crate names, module file paths, and build arrangement MUST NOT appear in any identity: an identity derived from layout rather than from declared facts is refused under the layout-derived-identity diagnostic.

<a id="GNT-34.9-standard-library-contract-versioning"></a>

**[GNT-34.9-standard-library-contract-versioning] Standard-library contract versioning.** The aggregate hierarchy publishes one versioned standard-library contract together with the package graph, prelude, facade identities, stability tiers, and applicability it was built from. A consumer that presents a contract version, package identity, or interface digest differing from the published one is refused under the contract-version-mismatch diagnostic rather than accepted, merged, or repaired, and a version change states its compatibility or incompatibility explicitly.

<a id="GNT-34.10-relocation-and-deprecation"></a>

**[GNT-34.10-relocation-and-deprecation] Relocation and deprecation.** A relocation names the old path, the new path, and the preserved defining identity, and a deprecation names the item, the tier it moves to, and the replacement if any. A relocation that changes item identity, that loses the old spelling without a declared migration, or that is not declared explicitly is refused under the invalid-relocation diagnostic. Deprecation never silently removes an item or widens its own stability tier.

<a id="GNT-34.11-aggregate-manifests-and-publication-inputs"></a>

**[GNT-34.11-aggregate-manifests-and-publication-inputs] Aggregate manifests and publication inputs.** The aggregate hierarchy publishes one manifest that lists every package with its class, tier, applicability, dependencies, and interface digest, and that manifest is the input downstream package tests, tooling, and publication consume. A manifest that omits a declared package, that carries an identity differing from the recomputed identity, or that is stale against the declaration is refused under the publication-drift diagnostic rather than merged into a publication.

<a id="GNT-34.12-standard-library-architecture-non-claims"></a>

**[GNT-34.12-standard-library-architecture-non-claims] Standard-library architecture non-claims.** This section does not implement any family behavior; does not define parser, formatter, linker, or tooling behavior; does not promise that any capability, provider, or adapter exists; does not make repository crate layout, filenames, or build arrangement source identity; and does not define package acquisition, registry trust, documentation rendering, or release policy. Model facts and tests MUST NOT be presented as such guarantees.

## 35. Scalar and Binary Foundation Values

<a id="GNT-35.0-scalar-and-binary-foundation"></a>

**[GNT-35.0-scalar-and-binary-foundation] Scalar and binary foundation.** This section defines an analyzer-only declaration model for the non-value `Never`, `Char`, fixed-width signed and unsigned integers of 8, 16, 32, and 64 bits, the logical octet `Byte`, immutable `Bytes`, and logically mutable `ByteBuffer`, together with their declared widths, canonical text, checked arithmetic and overflow modes, division and remainder, shifts, bounds, total order, stable hash, canonical encoding, initialized-prefix behavior, exclusive mutation, consuming freeze, copy and move independence, allocation quotas, and storage-strategy equivalence. Its pure model is `crates/gantry-ir/src/scalar.rs` and its analyzer evidence is `crates/gantry-conformance/tests/scalar_foundation.rs`. The frozen scalar diagnostics are `scalar-invalid-width` (`GNT-35.1`), `scalar-invalid-literal` (`GNT-35.2`), `scalar-overflow-refused` (`GNT-35.3`), `scalar-division-by-zero` (`GNT-35.4`), `scalar-invalid-shift` (`GNT-35.5`), `scalar-invalid-char` (`GNT-35.6`), `scalar-noncanonical-encoding` (`GNT-35.7`), `scalar-buffer-bounds` and `scalar-buffer-shared-mutation` (`GNT-35.8`), `scalar-cross-width-comparison` (`GNT-35.9`), `scalar-quota-exceeded` (`GNT-35.10`), `scalar-storage-strategy-divergence` (`GNT-35.11`), and `scalar-never-constructed` and `scalar-non-claim-as-guarantee` (`GNT-35.12`); each diagnostic names one owning clause and no spelling is shared by two refusal conditions. A refusal spelling has exactly one owning clause, and another clause invokes it only where this section states that it does. Every width, bound, and octet count here is a declared portable property: no Rust representation, target pointer width, host byte order, allocator, or spare capacity is observable, and no implicit arbitrary-precision semantics exist.

<a id="GNT-35.1-declared-widths-and-identity"></a>

**[GNT-35.1-declared-widths-and-identity] Declared widths and identity.** Every fixed-width integer is exactly its declared width on every target, and each of `Int8`, `Int16`, `Int32`, `Int64`, `UInt8`, `UInt16`, `UInt32`, `UInt64`, and `Byte` carries one distinct type identity. `Byte` is a logical octet in the inclusive range 0 through 255 and is not `UInt8`: no implicit conversion, comparison, or joining exists between them or between any two widths, and a declaration that presents a width, range, or identity differing from the declared one is refused under the invalid-width diagnostic. Decoding a fixed-width integer from an octet sequence whose length differs from the declared width is refused under that same invalid-width diagnostic: the octet count presents a width, so the attribution is deliberate rather than a literal or encoding refusal.

<a id="GNT-35.2-literal-formation-and-canonical-text"></a>

**[GNT-35.2-literal-formation-and-canonical-text] Literal formation and canonical text.** Canonical decimal text for a fixed-width integer is an optional sign followed by digits, with no leading zero on a multi-digit magnitude, no bare `+`, and no negative zero; a value outside the declared range is refused rather than truncated to it. Parsing preserves the presented identity exactly: text that is not the canonical spelling of the value it denotes is refused under the invalid-literal diagnostic, and formatting reproduces only canonical text.

<a id="GNT-35.3-checked-arithmetic-and-overflow-modes"></a>

**[GNT-35.3-checked-arithmetic-and-overflow-modes] Checked arithmetic and overflow modes.** Addition, subtraction, multiplication, negation, and conversion carry an explicit overflow mode — refuse, wrapping, or saturating — and the default is refuse. Under refuse, a result leaving the declared range is refused under the overflow-refused diagnostic; wrapping is modulo the declared width and saturating clamps to the declared bound, and neither is ever chosen implicitly by a target, build profile, or optimizer.

<a id="GNT-35.4-division-remainder-and-signed-semantics"></a>

**[GNT-35.4-division-remainder-and-signed-semantics] Division, remainder, and signed semantics.** Integer division truncates toward zero, the remainder takes the sign of the dividend, and a zero divisor is refused under the division-by-zero diagnostic for both operations. Negating the minimum value of a signed width and dividing that minimum by negative one leave the declared range and are refused under the overflow-refused diagnostic; no scalar operation produces an infinity, a not-a-number, or a silently clamped quotient.

<a id="GNT-35.5-shifts-and-numeric-bounds"></a>

**[GNT-35.5-shifts-and-numeric-bounds] Shifts and numeric bounds.** A shift amount must be at least zero and strictly less than the declared width; an amount at or beyond the width is refused under the invalid-shift diagnostic rather than masked, and no shift is defined for a negative amount. Left shifts obey the same explicit overflow mode as other arithmetic, right shifts are arithmetic for signed widths and logical for unsigned widths, and rotations, bit counting, and byte-order swaps are outside this section.

<a id="GNT-35.6-char-values-and-unicode-scalars"></a>

**[GNT-35.6-char-values-and-unicode-scalars] Char values and Unicode scalars.** `Char` holds exactly one Unicode scalar value: a code point in the inclusive range U+0000 through U+10FFFF that is not a surrogate. A code point outside that set, an unpaired surrogate, and a partial or over-long UTF-8 sequence are refused under the invalid-char diagnostic. `Char` performs no case mapping, normalization, collation, or width measurement, and its canonical text never depends on a process locale or host encoding. Decoding octets into a `Char` admits exactly one Unicode scalar value and refuses a partial, over-long, or surrogate encoding under the invalid-char diagnostic.

<a id="GNT-35.7-bytes-and-canonical-encoding"></a>

**[GNT-35.7-bytes-and-canonical-encoding] Bytes and canonical encoding.** `Bytes` is an immutable, sealed octet sequence of exactly its recorded length with no spare capacity in its identity. Canonical text is lowercase hexadecimal of even length, and text that is not the canonical spelling of the octets it denotes is refused under the noncanonical-encoding diagnostic; decoding to text requires well-formed UTF-8 and never transcodes implicitly. Sealing preserves byte identity, so two values are equal exactly when their octets are equal. The empty sequence is canonical and its canonical text is the empty string, and a read at or beyond the recorded length is refused under the buffer-bounds condition owned by `GNT-35.8`.

<a id="GNT-35.8-bytebuffer-mutation-and-freezing"></a>

**[GNT-35.8-bytebuffer-mutation-and-freezing] ByteBuffer mutation and freezing.** `ByteBuffer` exposes a logically mutable initialized prefix: length, octets, append, extend, truncate, and split are defined over initialized octets only, and no uninitialized or spare region is observable. Mutation requires unique ownership: aliasing a buffer refuses mutation of either alias under the shared-mutation diagnostic, while a deep copy is independent and survives mutation of the original. Aliasing marks the buffer shared permanently, and this section defines no unique-reclaim operation, so `independent_copy` is the only route that yields a buffer independent of the original. Freeze consumes the buffer into `Bytes`, and an index, split position, or length outside the initialized prefix is refused under the buffer-bounds diagnostic.

<a id="GNT-35.9-equality-order-and-stable-hash"></a>

**[GNT-35.9-equality-order-and-stable-hash] Equality, order, and stable hash.** Equality and ordering are defined only within one scalar kind: values of different kinds are never compared, coerced, or ordered together, and such an attempt is refused under the cross-width-comparison diagnostic. Within a kind, order is total over the declared range and a stable hash of the canonical encoding is identical across runs, processes, targets, and storage strategies.

<a id="GNT-35.10-allocation-quotas-and-cancellation"></a>

**[GNT-35.10-allocation-quotas-and-cancellation] Allocation quotas and cancellation.** Every buffer and sealed sequence is charged against a declared quota before its octets become live, truncation and split release the released charge, and a request that would exceed the ceiling is refused under the quota-exceeded diagnostic with no partial growth visible. Cancellation between any two operations leaves each buffer at an initialized-prefix boundary with its charges consistent, so a cancelled operation is indistinguishable from one that never began. A quota presented with a charge beyond its ceiling is refused under the quota-exceeded diagnostic rather than silently clamped, and a split conserves the total charge by retaining any charge not assigned to the tail on the head.

<a id="GNT-35.11-storage-strategy-equivalence-and-round-trips"></a>

**[GNT-35.11-storage-strategy-equivalence-and-round-trips] Storage-strategy equivalence and round trips.** Eager-copy, copy-on-write, and storage-reuse implementations of these values produce identical octets, identical quota charges, identical refusals, and identical canonical text for the same operation sequence; physical work differs and is nonsemantic, so no observable behavior may depend on it, and any divergence is refused under the storage-strategy-divergence diagnostic. Canonical text, external encodings, and recovery projections round-trip exactly, and a projection that loses an octet, a width, or an identity is refused rather than repaired.

<a id="GNT-35.12-scalar-and-binary-non-claims"></a>

**[GNT-35.12-scalar-and-binary-non-claims] Scalar and binary non-claims.** This section does not define raw memory, address-space layout, allocator behavior, spare capacity, uninitialized storage, or pointer and FFI representation; does not promise source literal parsing, formatter policy, or presentation formatting; does not introduce implicit arbitrary-precision arithmetic; and does not define codecs, compression, or cryptography. No scalar value is ever constructed, encoded, journaled, or observed for `Never`, and an attempt to do so is refused under the never-constructed diagnostic; presenting any non-claim here as a guarantee is refused under the non-claim-as-guarantee diagnostic, and model facts and tests MUST NOT be presented as such guarantees.

## 36. Recursive Algebraic Data Types, Aliases, Visibility, and Constants

<a id="GNT-36.0-recursive-algebraic-data-types"></a>

**[GNT-36.0-recursive-algebraic-data-types] Recursive algebraic data types.** This section defines an analyzer-only declaration model for named algebraic data types with declared constructors, tags, and fields; directly recursive and mutually recursive declarations; type aliases and their resolution; declaration and reference visibility; destructuring patterns with constructor identity; match coverage over the declared constructor space; bounded effect-free constant values built from finite constructor trees; package-load non-execution for declarations; canonical schema closure; boundary-encoding independence; and durable round trips. Its pure model is `crates/gantry-ir/src/adt.rs` and its analyzer evidence is `crates/gantry-conformance/tests/adt_foundation.rs`. The frozen ADT diagnostics are `adt-duplicate-constructor` and `adt-constructor-arity` (`GNT-36.1`), `adt-unproductive-recursion` (`GNT-36.2`), `adt-unresolved-reference` (`GNT-36.3`), `adt-alias-cycle` and `adt-alias-arity` (`GNT-36.4`), `adt-invisible-reference` (`GNT-36.5`), `adt-unknown-constructor` and `adt-pattern-shape` (`GNT-36.6`), `adt-incomplete-match` (`GNT-36.7`), `adt-constant-form` and `adt-constant-limit` (`GNT-36.8`), `adt-mutable-global` (`GNT-36.9`), `adt-schema-divergence` (`GNT-36.10`), `adt-round-trip-loss` (`GNT-36.11`), and `adt-non-claim-as-guarantee` (`GNT-36.12`); each diagnostic names one owning clause and no spelling is shared by two refusal conditions. Declarations carry no bodies, no initializers, and no effect-capable members, constant values admitted here are finite constructor trees whose effect, cycle, overflow, and general limit rules stay owned by `GNT-32.8` and `GNT-32.9`, and no declaration in this section executes at package load.

<a id="GNT-36.1-declaration-and-constructor-identity"></a>

**[GNT-36.1-declaration-and-constructor-identity] Declaration and constructor identity.** A type declares one name, one visibility, one parameter list, and one or more constructors; a constructor declares one name, one tag, and one field list whose entries name declared types. A duplicate type name in one package, a duplicate constructor name inside one type, and a duplicate tag inside one type are refused under the duplicate-constructor diagnostic. Every constructor of one type carries that type's exact parameter list, and a constructor whose parameter list, field count, or tag range departs from its declaration is refused under the constructor-arity diagnostic. A parameter list is identity only: a parameter name is never a type reference, and a field entry names a declared type or a scalar leaf, so a field spelling that names a declared parameter and no declaration is refused under the unresolved-reference diagnostic. Constructor identity is the tuple of package, type name, constructor name, tag, and ordered field type names; it is never derived from a boundary encoding, a wire tag, a declaration position, or a declaration order.

<a id="GNT-36.2-guarded-productive-recursion"></a>

**[GNT-36.2-guarded-productive-recursion] Guarded and productive recursion.** A declaration set MAY be directly or mutually recursive, and recursion through a constructor field is the only admitted recursion. Every declared type MUST be inhabited by at least one finite value: a constructor is buildable when every one of its field types is buildable, and a type with no buildable constructor is refused under the unproductive-recursion diagnostic rather than admitted as an empty type. Refusal is deterministic and atomic: a refused declaration set yields no partial model, no partially published constructor identity, and no schema.

<a id="GNT-36.3-mutual-recursion-and-order-independence"></a>

**[GNT-36.3-mutual-recursion-and-order-independence] Mutual recursion and order independence.** Declarations are order-independent: a reference to a type declared later in the same package resolves identically to a reference to a type declared earlier, and mutual recursion is admitted without forward-declaration syntax. A reference naming a type that no declaration in the package provides is refused under the unresolved-reference diagnostic. The canonical schema of a declaration set is byte-identical for every declaration order and every declaration position.

<a id="GNT-36.4-aliases-and-alias-cycles"></a>

**[GNT-36.4-aliases-and-alias-cycles] Aliases and alias cycles.** An alias names one declared type or alias with the same parameter list and resolves transitively to a declaration. An alias carries its resolved target's exact parameter list, and an alias whose parameter list departs from its resolved target is refused under the alias-arity diagnostic. Alias resolution terminates, and a cycle in the alias-only relation is refused under the alias-cycle diagnostic. An alias never creates a second identity for its target: constructor identity, pattern matching, match coverage, and schema closure see the resolved target, so an alias and its target are interchangeable in every checked position.

<a id="GNT-36.5-visibility-and-reference-admission"></a>

**[GNT-36.5-visibility-and-reference-admission] Visibility and reference admission.** Visibility is private to the declaring module, package-visible, or public. A reference is admitted only when the referenced declaration is at least as open as the referencing site; a reference that reaches a less open declaration is refused under the invisible-reference diagnostic, and a public declaration whose field, alias, or constructor exposes a less open declaration is refused under the same diagnostic. Visibility never changes constructor identity, canonical schema, or match coverage.

<a id="GNT-36.6-destructuring-and-pattern-identity"></a>

**[GNT-36.6-destructuring-and-pattern-identity] Destructuring and pattern identity.** A pattern names one constructor of the matched type and carries exactly one sub-pattern per declared field of that constructor; a pattern naming a constructor that the matched type does not declare is refused under the unknown-constructor diagnostic, and a pattern whose sub-pattern count departs from the declared field count is refused under the constructor-arity diagnostic. A sub-pattern whose field type resolves to a declared type is a constructor pattern naming one constructor of that type, and a sub-pattern whose field type resolves to a scalar leaf is a scalar form that carries no constructor; a scalar form is admissible at any field position and covers that field's whole subtree, and a constructor form in a scalar leaf position is refused under the pattern-shape diagnostic. Pattern matching compares constructor identity, never tag arithmetic, declaration position, or boundary shape, so two constructors with the same spelling on different types remain distinct and are never matched by one pattern.

<a id="GNT-36.7-match-coverage-and-exhaustiveness"></a>

**[GNT-36.7-match-coverage-and-exhaustiveness] Match coverage and exhaustiveness.** A match over a type is complete when every constructor the type declares is covered and every sub-pattern covers its field type; the first uncovered constructor path is refused under the incomplete-match diagnostic. Coverage is computed over the declared constructor space and not over a boundary encoding, a tag range, a default case, or recovery eligibility, and a type with exactly one constructor still requires that constructor to be covered.

<a id="GNT-36.8-bounded-constant-values"></a>

**[GNT-36.8-bounded-constant-values] Bounded constant values.** A constant site declares one finite constructor tree of its declared type: constructor nodes with exactly one argument per declared field and scalar leaves. A site whose value is deferred, unfolded at load, or otherwise not a finite constructor tree is refused under the constant-form diagnostic, and each site is charged for its node count and depth before publication, where a site exceeding its declared budget is refused under the constant-limit diagnostic with no partially charged or partially published site. Effect, cycle, overflow, and general evaluation-limit rules for constants remain owned by `GNT-32.8` and `GNT-32.9`, and a constant publishes its canonical value only after charging succeeds.

<a id="GNT-36.9-package-load-non-execution"></a>

**[GNT-36.9-package-load-non-execution] Package-load non-execution.** No declaration in this section executes at package load: declaring a type, an alias, or a constant site runs no source statement, admits no hidden initializer, and admits no mutable package global, whose declaration is refused under the mutable-global diagnostic. Every declaration's package-load fact is declaration-only, so the number of executed statements and the number of executed declarations are zero by construction rather than by convention.

<a id="GNT-36.10-schema-closure-and-boundary-independence"></a>

**[GNT-36.10-schema-closure-and-boundary-independence] Schema closure and boundary independence.** The canonical schema is closed over declarations — type names, parameter lists, constructors, tags, field types, aliases, constant sites, and visibility — and is computed deterministically, ordered by declared name and tag. Boundary labels, external spellings, codec tags, host order, and storage order are nonsemantic: two declaration sets that differ only in boundary labels have identical constructor identity and byte-identical canonical schema, and a schema that depends on a boundary encoding, a host, or a storage order is refused under the schema-divergence diagnostic.

<a id="GNT-36.11-durable-round-trips-and-interface-identity"></a>

**[GNT-36.11-durable-round-trips-and-interface-identity] Durable round trips and interface identity.** A durable projection of a declaration set carries every type, constructor, tag, field type, parameter, alias, constant site, and visibility, together with the package identity it belongs to. Rebuilding from a projection yields an equal model with identical constructor identity, canonical schema, and match coverage, and a projection that omits, reorders, or alters any carried declaration is refused under the round-trip-loss diagnostic rather than repaired, defaulted, or partially applied.

<a id="GNT-36.12-adt-non-claims"></a>

**[GNT-36.12-adt-non-claims] ADT non-claims.** This section does not define runtime representation, memory layout, allocation, sharing, or cyclic runtime values; does not define dynamic dispatch, trait solving, or effect inference; does not define boundary wire formats, codecs, or serialization spellings; does not admit hidden initializers, mutable package globals, or source execution at package load; and does not weaken `GNT-36.2`, so recursion is never admitted unguarded or unproductive. No declared type, constructor, or constant here is validated by a boundary encoding or by recovery eligibility, and presenting any non-claim here as a guarantee is refused under the non-claim-as-guarantee diagnostic.

## 37. Callable Values, Captures, Reuse Kinds, and Frame Admission

<a id="GNT-37.0-callable-values-and-frame-admission"></a>

**[GNT-37.0-callable-values-and-frame-admission] Callable values and frame admission.** This section defines an analyzer-only contract for first-class callable values: reuse kinds, canonical shape, explicit captures with modes, bounded shape, name, capture, and logical-frame budgets, admission and settlement transitions, effect rows over captured callables, canonical identity, and a durable capture projection. It retires the earlier statement that closure types remain unadmitted, which `GNT-3-T-GENERIC-CALL` now records as the Section 37 contract instead of a blanket exclusion. Its pure model is `crates/gantry-ir/src/callable.rs` and its analyzer evidence is `crates/gantry-conformance/tests/callable_foundation.rs`. The frozen callable diagnostics are `callable-shape-refused` (`GNT-37.1`), `callable-frame-limit` (`GNT-37.2`), `callable-capture-refused` (`GNT-37.3`), `callable-reuse-refused` (`GNT-37.4`), `callable-settlement-refused` (`GNT-37.5`), `callable-effect-erasure` (`GNT-37.6`), `callable-durable-capture` (`GNT-37.7`), `callable-round-trip-loss` (`GNT-37.8`), `callable-type-unadmitted` (`GNT-37.0`), `callable-expression-unadmitted` (`GNT-37.0`), `callable-invocation-unadmitted` (`GNT-37.10`), and `callable-reference-unadmitted` (`GNT-37.0`); each diagnostic names one owning clause and no spelling is shared by two refusal conditions. This section admits the source callable type form in a signature annotation, which is a parameter or result annotation of a function, method, or trait-method declaration whose parameter and result positions all name closed types and whose declaration is neither the entry point nor an action declaration, and in a binding annotation, which is the annotation of a `let` binding, and admits no source callable expression into an analyzed artifact: the parser recognises the annotation form and the callable expression form `fn(<name>: <type>, ...) -> <type> { <body> }`, an admitted annotation resolves to the canonical callable type of its reuse kind, ordered parameter types, and result type, and analysis refuses every other occurrence of either form, and every callable type that a generic call reaches as an instantiation argument, that it reaches with `callable-type-unadmitted` (`GNT-37.0`) or `callable-expression-unadmitted` (`GNT-37.0`), refusing an expression before its body is typed or lowered while a diagnostic of the refused body's own annotations may accompany the refusal, and an occurrence that is itself unreachable code is refused by the reachability rule rather than by either refusal, so the section defines no admitted source callable expression, no source callable value, no runtime representation or native frame layout, no dynamic dispatch, and no ambient capture. A name that denotes a declared callable or a declared action is not a value derivation outside the admitted binding form: a declared callable is reached through a direct call, through the initializer of a binding whose annotation is a callable type, and through an invocation of such a binding, and a declared action through its operation form, so analysis refuses such a name in every other position that requires a value under `callable-reference-unadmitted` (`GNT-37.0`), reports the identifier in an `identifier` field, and never types the name as the declaration's callable value, while the callee position of a direct call keeps the meaning this section leaves unchanged.

Every source callable type form has exactly one occurrence class, reported in an `occurrence` field when the form is refused: `signature` for a parameter or result annotation of a function, method, or trait-method declaration whose parameter and result positions all name closed types and whose declaration is neither the entry point nor an action declaration, which this section admits; `binding-annotation` for the annotation of a `let` binding, which this section admits for a binding whose value is a callable-typed value with no runtime representation, and whose invocation form admits only a binding that holds one declared callable as its value; `boundary-position` for a parameter or result annotation of the entry point or of an action declaration, whose types are boundary schema roots and which this section refuses; `open-member` for a signature annotation whose parameter or result position does not name a closed type, which this section refuses because `GNT-37.1` requires every parameter and result position to name a closed type, and which equally covers a binding annotation whose parameter or result position does not name a closed type; `non-signature` for an annotation that is not a parameter or result annotation of a callable declaration and is not a binding annotation, which this section refuses because no admitted position reaches it; `instantiation-argument` for a callable type that a generic call reaches as a complete instantiation argument or as one of its members, which this section refuses because the template type-expression grammar cannot name a callable type and no instantiation of a callable type is admitted; and `nested-component` for a type form that is a component of another type expression, which includes a generic argument and a parameter or result position of an enclosing callable form. The classes are disjoint and cover every reachable occurrence, so an admitted class is never a refused class and no occurrence class is inferred from a call site, a boundary encoding, or a recovery outcome.

<a id="GNT-37.1-reuse-kinds-and-canonical-shape"></a>

**[GNT-37.1-reuse-kinds-and-canonical-shape] Reuse kinds and canonical shape.** A callable value declares exactly one reuse kind, which is `Fn`, `FnMut`, or `FnOnce`, one ordered parameter list, one result type, and one body identity, and every parameter and result position names a closed type that capture, ownership, effect, and suspension decisions consume exactly rather than guess. A value whose kind, parameter order, or result departs from its declaration, and a shape that exceeds a declared shape budget, is refused under the shape-refused diagnostic. Callable identity is the tuple of reuse kind, ordered parameter type names, and result type name, and it is never derived from a boundary encoding, a native frame address, a capture plan, or a declaration position.

<a id="GNT-37.2-bounded-logical-frame-admission"></a>

**[GNT-37.2-bounded-logical-frame-admission] Bounded logical-frame admission.** Each call is admitted into a bounded logical frame: every admission charges exactly one frame, and a call whose depth is at or beyond the declared logical-frame budget is refused under the frame-limit diagnostic before any charge. Admission is deterministic and atomic: a refused admission retains no frame slot, publishes no partial value, and leaves the enclosing value's reuse state unchanged, and no admitted call consumes a native stack resource, recurses on the host stack, or reserves an unbounded frame.

<a id="GNT-37.3-explicit-captures-and-capture-plans"></a>

**[GNT-37.3-explicit-captures-and-capture-plans] Explicit captures and capture plans.** A capture plan carries zero or more capture descriptors, each naming one captured binding and one mode, which is `copy`, `move`, or `loan`, and the plan's descriptors are ordered by canonical binding name, so a plan's canonical encoding is byte-identical for every source-declaration order of the same captures. Ambient or inferred capture is not admitted: every capture is explicit. A descriptor with no binding name, a plan that repeats one binding, a descriptor or plan that exceeds a declared capture budget, and a capture that names no enclosing binding offered to the closure of its component row is refused under the capture-refused diagnostic, and no descriptor mode is defaulted or silently converted into another mode. A capture class assigns exactly one mode: a freely copyable binding is copied, a binding whose state is private to the callable or that is affine is moved, and a temporary loan is loaned only where the callable does not escape the statement that declares it, so a loan capture in an escaping callable is refused under the capture-refused diagnostic. Assignment is independent of the order in which bindings are offered, and no class is inferred from a call site, a boundary encoding, or a recovery outcome.

<a id="GNT-37.4-reuse-kinds-and-affine-consumption"></a>

**[GNT-37.4-reuse-kinds-and-affine-consumption] Reuse kinds and affine consumption.** A kind that holds exclusive capture state refuses an overlapping admission, a single-use kind is consumed at admission, and a consumed or poisoned value refuses further reuse; each of these refusals is reported under the reuse-refused diagnostic. Reuse refusal is decided before any frame charge and before any reuse-state change, and no reuse decision is inferred from a call site, a boundary shape, or a recovery outcome. A kind that is assigned rather than declared is the weakest of `Fn`, `FnMut`, and `FnOnce` that admits every assigned capture mode, so an assignment whose captures include an affine binding is single-use, an assignment whose captures include private or loaned state is exclusive, and an assignment whose captures are all freely copyable is freely reusable.

<a id="GNT-37.5-settlement-and-poisoning"></a>

**[GNT-37.5-settlement-and-poisoning] Settlement and poisoning.** Every admitted call settles at most once: a completed settlement and a typed domain-error settlement both leave a reusable kind reusable, while a failed or cancelled settlement poisons a kind that holds exclusive capture state, because that state may be partially settled, and leaves a kind whose captures are immutable reusable. A settlement of a call that was never admitted, that already settled, or that no longer belongs to a live admission is refused under the settlement-refused diagnostic, and a poisoned value never returns to a reusable state.

<a id="GNT-37.6-exact-effect-rows"></a>

**[GNT-37.6-exact-effect-rows] Effect rows over captured callables.** A callable value's row contains the effects of the callables it captures together with its own body effects, and a declared row MUST contain every effect of every component row it composes. The component row of one capture is the row of the enclosing binding that capture names, and the component row of a callable value is the union of the component rows of its captures, so a captured callable contributes its declared row, an ordinary captured value contributes the empty row, and a binding that no capture names contributes nothing because every capture is explicit; composition is a union and nothing else, so one value's component row is independent of the order in which enclosing bindings are offered. A row that omits, narrows, or erases a component effect is refused under the effect-erasure diagnostic rather than admitted as an approximation, and row closure is decided over declared rows and never over a call site's context, a boundary label, or recovery eligibility.

<a id="GNT-37.7-durable-capture-projection"></a>

**[GNT-37.7-durable-capture-projection] Durable capture projection.** A durable capture projection carries the value's reuse kind, ordered parameter types, result type, canonical identity, and every capture descriptor with its mode. A value with a live call, with a consumed or poisoned reuse state, or with a loan capture is refused under the durable-capture diagnostic rather than partially projected, and no projection is repaired, defaulted, or completed from the source spelling.

<a id="GNT-37.8-durable-round-trips-and-identity"></a>

**[GNT-37.8-durable-round-trips-and-identity] Durable round trips and identity.** Rebuilding a live value from a projection yields a value whose canonical encoding and identity equal those of the projected value. A projection that no longer encodes the identity it carries, because a descriptor was dropped, altered, reordered, or added, is refused under the round-trip-loss diagnostic rather than repaired or partially applied, and a carried identity is compared with a recomputed canonical encoding instead of being trusted as a self-consistent claim.

<a id="GNT-37.9-canonical-encoding-and-order-independence"></a>

**[GNT-37.9-canonical-encoding-and-order-independence] Canonical encoding and order independence.** A callable value's canonical encoding is computed deterministically from its reuse kind, ordered parameter type names, result type name, body identity, and capture descriptors in canonical binding order. The encoding is injective and length-prefixed, so two distinct values never share an encoding and no boundary split or concatenation makes two distinct values encode identically. Boundary labels, host order, storage order, and native frame addresses are nonsemantic, and no callable encoding depends on them.

<a id="GNT-37.10-direct-call-and-receiver-compatibility"></a>

**[GNT-37.10-direct-call-and-receiver-compatibility] Direct-call and receiver compatibility.** Existing direct calls and the v1 receiver meaning are unchanged: this section introduces one admitted invocation form whose callee names a binding that holds one declared callable as its value, and no other new call form, no receiver rule, and no re-typing of an existing direct call, and the direct-call effect fixed point of `GNT-3-T-EFFECTS` remains the owner of direct-call effect closure. Admitting a callable value admits no operation, capability, host-family contract, or standard-library package edge by itself, so declaring or holding a callable never widens the authority of the site that holds it. Because this section introduces no call form beyond the admitted binding form, a call whose callee names a binding that holds one declared callable as its value is admitted as a direct call with that identity and contributes the callee's row exactly as a direct call does, while a call whose callee denotes any other callable value rather than a declared callable has no derivation: analysis refuses it under `callable-invocation-unadmitted` (`GNT-37.10`), reports the callee's reuse kind in a `reuse_kind` field, and types the refused call as the callee's declared result before any of the call's own arguments are typed, so the refusal replaces the call's typing instead of mistyping the call as its callee. The row contract of `GNT-3-T-EFFECT-ROWS` applies to every invocation form this section admits, and every other callable value can be declared, passed, and held but not invoked.

<a id="GNT-37.11-refusal-discipline-and-atomicity"></a>

**[GNT-37.11-refusal-discipline-and-atomicity] Refusal discipline and atomicity.** Each callable refusal names exactly one owning clause through one diagnostic spelling, and no spelling is shared by two refusal conditions. Every refusal here is deterministic and atomic: a refused value publishes no partial identity, retains no frame slot, admits no capture, and leaves no partially settled state, and one declaration set yields the same refusals for every host, boundary encoding, and evaluation strategy.

<a id="GNT-37.12-callable-non-claims"></a>
A name that denotes a declared callable or a declared action is refused as a value under `callable-reference-unadmitted` (`GNT-37.0`) in every position but a binding initializer and an invocation of such a binding, so this section admits no source reference form beyond that binding form.
**[GNT-37.12-callable-non-claims] Callable non-claims.** This section does not admit source-level closure syntax, source-level closure inference, or a source-level capture boundary: the parser recognises the callable expression form and analysis refuses every occurrence it reaches before the body is typed or lowered, so the capture classes that drive mode assignment are declared by an analyzer instead of read from source; does not define runtime representation, memory layout, allocation, native frame layout, or host stack growth; does not admit dynamic dispatch, trait solving, effect inference, or ambient capture; does not admit escaping loans or loans that cross a forbidden suspension; does not admit native-stack recursion; and does not define boundary wire formats or serialization spellings for callables. It does not weaken `GNT-37.4`, `GNT-37.6`, or `GNT-37.7`, so no callable here is admitted with an ambiguous reuse state, an erased component row, or a partially projected durable form.

## 38. Typed Errors, Assertions, Panic, and Divergence

<a id="GNT-38.0-error-and-divergence-scope"></a>

**[GNT-38.0-error-and-divergence-scope] Error and divergence scope.** This section defines the source-level error, assertion, panic, and divergence contract that the preceding sections do not own: typed domain-error propagation, source-level error-conversion traits, checked assertions, panic, unreachable paths, and the uninhabited type `Never` with its dedicated divergence completion rule. Its pure model is `crates/gantry-ir/src/error_semantics.rs` and its analyzer evidence is `crates/gantry-conformance/tests/error_semantics.rs`. The frozen diagnostics of this section are `failure-channel-conversion-refused` (`GNT-38.0`), `error-propagation-refused` (`GNT-38.1`), `error-conversion-refused` (`GNT-38.1`), `panic-path-refused` (`GNT-38.2`), `panic-frame-limit` (`GNT-38.2`), `divergence-unconstrained` (`GNT-38.3`), `never-boundary-refused` (`GNT-38.4`), `never-durable-refused` (`GNT-38.4`), and `never-signature-refused` (`GNT-38.4`); each diagnostic names one owning clause and no spelling is shared by two refusal conditions. A typed domain error is distinct from operational failure, policy denial, cancellation, journal failure, resource exhaustion, adapter failure, and unknown external outcome, and no form this section admits converts one of those channels into another: the channel vocabulary of `crates/gantry-ir/src/error_semantics.rs` is closed, and every refusal of this section reports the channel it concerns. The channel vocabulary is the contract-level vocabulary of this section and does not replace the runtime outcome categories or the operation ABI failure classes: the mapping from a channel onto the runtime or host spelling that reports it is published by the slice that wires outcomes, so this section claims no runtime spelling of its own.

<a id="GNT-38.1-typed-error-propagation"></a>

**[GNT-38.1-typed-error-propagation] Typed error propagation.** A propagation operand propagates a typed domain error out of the enclosing callable only through a declared conversion from the operand error type into the enclosing callable error type: analysis admits the operand where exactly one such conversion is declared, types the enclosing callable result at its declared error type, and refuses every other operand under `error-propagation-refused`, naming the operand error type and the enclosing result type in the refusal instead of guessing a conversion. A conversion is declared by one implementation of the conversion trait `ErrorConversion`, whose receiver names one concrete error type and whose single method returns one concrete error type, is total on its declared domain, keeps the channel of the operand, and is refused under `error-conversion-refused` when it is ambiguous, partial, or widens a channel, so no catch-all conversion of an operational failure, a policy denial, a cancellation, a journal failure, an exhaustion, an adapter failure, or an unknown external outcome into a domain error exists. Propagation preserves affine ownership exactly: the succeeded path discharges every must-consume obligation the operand carries, the refused path publishes no partial value, and no obligation is discharged twice.

<a id="GNT-38.2-assertions-and-panic"></a>

**[GNT-38.2-assertions-and-panic] Assertions and panic.** A checked assertion is a source form whose operand is exactly `Bool`, whose success continues with the enclosing path, and whose failure settles as a typed failure outcome of the enclosing callable; analysis refuses an operand of any other type under `panic-path-refused` and never converts the operand or the failure into a domain error. A panic is a source form that never completes normally and settles as the failure outcome of the enclosing callable. Neither form introduces a host unwind across a task boundary or a public API boundary: the conversion of an integration failure and of a Gantry invariant failure at those boundaries remains owned by the fault-containment clauses, and this section only requires that the source forms reach them. The logical frames a panic reports are bounded by the declared panic-frame budget: a path whose reported frames would exceed that budget is refused under `panic-frame-limit` before any frame is charged rather than reporting an unbounded stack, so the panic diagnostics of this section are bounded and stable. A panic and a failed assertion lower to the same nonreturning form and settle as the failure outcome of the enclosing callable, which the machine reports through the outcome spelling its own vocabulary publishes; a non-`String` panic operand and a non-`Bool` assertion operand are refused under `panic-path-refused` with a `reason` field of `operand-type`. Both forms preserve affine obligations through their own nonreturning path exactly as an ordinary nonreturning path does, and neither form is admitted after hard cancellation.

<a id="GNT-38.3-divergence-and-never"></a>

**[GNT-38.3-divergence-and-never] Divergence and `Never`.** `Never` is an uninhabited type: no value of it exists, no runtime representation is admitted, and no expression constructs or observes one. An expression whose every normal completion is a nonreturning form has exactly one type, `Never`, and that type arises from the dedicated divergence completion rule of branch joining, which types an expression by the types of its value-producing completions and yields `Never` when none exists; divergence is never an implicit conversion of `Never` into another type and never a general subtyping relation. A use whose surviving type the completions do not determine is refused under `divergence-unconstrained` instead of guessing, so divergence never constrains a surviving result type, a generic argument, a boundary type, or an underconstrained call, and divergence propagates by the same rule through branches, loops, closures, and generic bodies.

<a id="GNT-38.4-boundaries-durability-and-non-claims"></a>

**[GNT-38.4-boundaries-durability-and-non-claims] Boundaries, durability, and non-claims.** No boundary declaration admits a `Never` position: a parameter or result annotation of an entry point, an action declaration, a capability declaration, or an operation declaration whose type is `Never` or contains it is refused under `never-boundary-refused`, because a boundary value must be constructible, encodable, and observable; every other signature position, which is a parameter or result annotation of a function, method, or trait-method declaration, is refused under `never-signature-refused` before any type expression is built, because no canonical form of the uninhabited type exists. No durable state carries a `Never` component: a checkpoint, a durable projection, a recovery record, or a carried identity that would contain one is refused under `never-durable-refused` rather than partially projected, repaired, or defaulted. This section introduces no native exception, no catch-all conversion of an operational failure into a domain error, no implicit `Never` subtyping, no source destructor, no cleanup after hard cancellation, no unbounded stack capture, no new effect, and no runtime type solving or recovery decoder, and it does not weaken the fault-containment clauses, the runtime outcome vocabulary, or the callable clauses; a refusal of this section is deterministic and atomic, publishes no partial value, and reports one diagnostic naming its owning clause.

## 39. Collection Key and Canonical Order Foundation

<a id="GNT-39.0-collection-key-and-order-scope"></a>

**[GNT-39.0-collection-key-and-order-scope] Collection key and order scope.** This section defines the collection key contract a source collection consumes: the admitted key domain, the canonical order, and duplicate-key identity. Its pure model is `crates/gantry-ir/src/collections.rs` and its analyzer evidence is `crates/gantry-conformance/tests/collections_foundation.rs`. The frozen diagnostics of this section are `collection-invalid-key` (`GNT-39.1`), `collection-duplicate-key` (`GNT-39.2`), `collection-non-claim-as-guarantee` (`GNT-39.3`), and `collection-type-unadmitted` (`GNT-39.4`); each diagnostic names one owning clause and no spelling is shared by two clauses. This section introduces no collection vocabulary beyond the recognised `Map<K, V>`, `Set<K>`, and `Range<T>` collection type forms of `GNT-39.4-map-type-form-recognition` and the `Map`, `Set`, and `Range` value model with its accounting, carriage, replacement, and traversal forms of `GNT-39.8-collection-value-model`: no source collection value, operation, iterator, stepping, traversal, or mutation rule, no family behavior, and no storage, layout, or performance fact, and it does not weaken `GNT-5.15-canonical-scalar-keys`: the framing, length, scalar-range, and UTF-8 refusals of the canonical scalar-key contract remain owned there and are not re-spelled here.

<a id="GNT-39.1-admitted-collection-keys"></a>

**[GNT-39.1-admitted-collection-keys] Admitted collection keys.** A collection key is exactly one admitted canonical scalar key of the implementation canonical scalar-key format version 1.0: normalized `Unit`, `Bool`, `Int`, finite normalized `Float`, or `String`. A candidate of any other kind — including `Decision`, `OperationError`, an option or result value, a list, a tuple, a struct, or an enum — is refused under `collection-invalid-key`, naming the refused kind, rather than coerced, encoded structurally, admitted through an application codec, or admitted through ordinary equality. Admission performs no cross-numeric-type coercion and grants no hashability beyond the admitted domain, and an admitted key carries the canonical frame, identity, and stable content hash of `GNT-5.15-canonical-scalar-keys` unchanged.

<a id="GNT-39.2-canonical-collection-order-and-duplicate-identity"></a>

**[GNT-39.2-canonical-collection-order-and-duplicate-identity] Canonical collection order and duplicate identity.** Collection order is the scalar-key order of `GNT-5.15-canonical-scalar-keys`: `Unit < Bool < Int < Float < String`, `false` before `true`, `Int` and `Float` in numeric order independently with no cross-numeric coercion, and `String` in lexicographic Unicode-scalar order. Comparison reports equal exactly when the admitted logical values compare equal, so normalized signed zeros have one `Float` key, and the order is the admitted logical value order rather than frame-byte order, content hashes, host order, or authored spelling. Duplicate identity uses that comparison rather than content hashes: a batch that admits two keys of equal identity is refused under `collection-duplicate-key`, the refusal reports the zero-based first and first-repeated input indices, and admission publishes no output unless every key is admitted and every identity is unique.

<a id="GNT-39.3-collection-foundation-non-claims"></a>

**[GNT-39.3-collection-foundation-non-claims] Collection-foundation non-claims.** This section claims nothing beyond the key contract above, the recognised collection type forms of `GNT-39.4-map-type-form-recognition`, and the collection type identities of `GNT-39.5-map-type-identity`, the `Set` and `Range` identities of `GNT-39.6-set-and-range-type-identities`, the sealed range step contract of `GNT-39.7-range-step-contract`, the `Map`, `Set`, and `Range` value model of `GNT-39.8-collection-value-model`: it admits no source collection value, operation, or collection API and no collection type whose form that clause does not recognise; does not define a range iteration protocol, iterator ownership or invalidation, mutation, an exhaustion diagnostic, suspension, quotas, schemas, recovery, or durable behavior; does not claim family behavior, performance, storage layout, or physical representation; and defines no boundary encoding beyond the canonical key frame it consumes. Presenting a model fact of this section as a guarantee it does not make is refused under `collection-non-claim-as-guarantee`, an unasserted declared non-claim carries that same frozen spelling from that one clause, and every declared non-claim must be asserted while none may be presented as a guarantee.

<a id="GNT-39.4-map-type-form-recognition"></a>

**[GNT-39.4-map-type-form-recognition] Map type-form recognition.** The grammar recognises exactly three collection type forms: `Map<K, V>`, a constructed value type with two argument types, and `Set<K>` and `Range<T>`, each a constructed value type with one argument type; every other reserved collection spelling is recognised as no form, and a source use of one is refused by the grammar. The three forms are admitted as constructed value types: analysis types an occurrence as the identity `GNT-39.5-map-type-identity` or `GNT-39.6-set-and-range-type-identities` publishes and builds the descriptor through that identity, so the key rule, the member rule, and the canonical text keep one owner, and an occurrence whose key or element argument that clause refuses is refused by it instead. The `collection-type-unadmitted` refusal of this clause narrows to the three conditions this edition does not admit: an occurrence whose argument the type phase resolves to no type at all; an occurrence in a boundary or signature position — a parameter, result, action, struct-field, enum-variant, struct-declaration-header, or enum-declaration-header annotation — because this edition publishes no boundary schema and no value for a collection type; and an occurrence whose `Map` value member or `Range` element names a collection type, which the owning identity refuses by its own member rule and this clause reports under its own spelling. None of the three conditions publishes a fact, a descriptor, or a type expression. The forms' argument positions are parsed and resolved as value types, so a malformed, empty, or mismatched argument list is refused by the grammar rather than by this clause, and this clause admits no collection value, construction, projection, iteration, mutation, boundary schema, or durable behavior.

<a id="GNT-39.5-map-type-identity"></a>

**[GNT-39.5-map-type-identity] Map type identity.** The recognised `Map<K, V>` form of `GNT-39.4-map-type-form-recognition` publishes one type identity: exactly two argument types in order, the key argument then the value argument, rendered as the canonical constructed-type text `Map<K,V>` over the canonical text of each argument. The key argument must denote exactly one admitted collection key type of `GNT-39.1-admitted-collection-keys` — `Unit`, `Bool`, `Int`, `Float`, or `String` — and an occurrence whose resolved key argument denotes any other type, including `Decision`, `OperationError`, the uninhabited type, an option, result, list, tuple, callable, or declared type, is refused under `collection-invalid-key`, naming the refused argument, rather than being coerced, structurally encoded, or admitted through ordinary equality; an occurrence whose key argument is admitted is admitted as this identity's constructed value type, and an occurrence whose key argument the type phase resolves to no type at all, or whose annotation appears in a boundary or signature position, keeps the `collection-type-unadmitted` refusal. The canonical text is exact in both directions: this section admits exactly one decoding of it, the two member texts in order, a key member text that names one of the five admitted key types, and a value member text that is the canonical text of one admitted value type. The key member rule applies before this one: a key member text that is not exactly one of those five admitted key types is refused under `collection-invalid-key`, naming the refused member, even when the same text is also non-canonical or carries a member this edition does not admit, and any other text that is not the canonical rendering of one identity — a non-canonical spelling, an unadmitted member, or a nested `Map` member — is refused under `collection-type-unadmitted`, this clause consuming those two frozen spellings of `GNT-39.0-collection-key-and-order-scope` rather than defining new ones. Decoding publishes the identity and nothing more. The identity is published and no `Map` value is: this clause admits no construction, projection, iteration, traversal, mutation, quota, schema, recovery, durability, boundary encoding, boundary schema, or lowering, defines no machine representation, and claims no family behavior, storage layout, or physical performance.

<a id="GNT-39.6-set-and-range-type-identities"></a>

**[GNT-39.6-set-and-range-type-identities] Set and Range type identities.** The one-argument collection type forms of `GNT-39.4-map-type-form-recognition` publish one identity each. A `Set<K>` identity is its element argument, which must denote exactly one admitted collection key type of `GNT-39.1-admitted-collection-keys` — `Unit`, `Bool`, `Int`, `Float`, or `String` — because a set element is a collection key: an occurrence whose resolved element argument denotes any other type is refused under `collection-invalid-key`, naming the refused argument, rather than being coerced, structurally encoded, or admitted through ordinary equality, and an occurrence whose element argument is admitted is admitted as that identity's constructed value type, while an occurrence whose element argument the type phase resolves to no type at all, or whose annotation appears in a boundary or signature position, keeps the `collection-type-unadmitted` refusal. A `Range<T>` identity is its element argument, which is any admitted value type that names no collection type anywhere inside it, and no stepping, bounds, ordering, or iteration rule is published with it. Both identities are rendered as the canonical constructed-type text `Set<K>` and `Range<T>` over the canonical text of the argument, and each is rendered and decoded exactly: for a `Set<K>`, an element member text that is not exactly one of those five admitted key types is refused under `collection-invalid-key` naming the whole refused member, even when the text is also non-canonical or carries a member this edition does not admit, and for either form any other text that is not the canonical rendering of one identity is refused under `collection-type-unadmitted`. The identities are published and no `Set` or `Range` value is: this clause admits no construction, projection, bounds, step, traversal, iteration, mutation, quota, schema, recovery, durability, boundary encoding, boundary schema, or lowering, defines no machine representation, and claims no family behavior, storage layout, or physical performance.

<a id="GNT-39.7-range-step-contract"></a>

**[GNT-39.7-range-step-contract] Sealed range step contract.** A range element type admits stepping exactly when this clause declares a step contract for it, and the contract is sealed: this clause declares every admitted step contract, and no package, adapter, host, or later declaration may define, extend, override, or infer one. Exactly one element type is admitted in this edition: `Int`, whose step is exactly one element value toward the bound, taken with the checked arithmetic of `GNT-35.3-checked-arithmetic-and-overflow-modes`, so that no wrapping, saturation, coercion, floating step, or host integer behavior is admitted. A range is ordered by the canonical element order of `GNT-39.2-canonical-collection-order-and-duplicate-identity`: its start bound is inclusive and its end bound exclusive, an unbounded side has no bound value there, and the two bounds are compared in that order. A forward step from a value is admitted exactly while its result lands strictly below an exclusive end bound and the checked successor exists, and a backward step exactly while its result is at or above an inclusive start bound and the checked predecessor exists; a step that would leave either the bound or the element's canonical value range is exhaustion rather than a refusal, a wrap, or a trap. Stepping is deterministic: the same value, direction, and bounds always produce the same outcome, with no dependence on host, target, mode, execution strategy, timing, or prior steps. This clause publishes the step contract only: it admits no `Range` value of its own and no construction, bound synthesis, traversal, iteration, loop integration, mutation, ownership or invalidation, an exhaustion diagnostic, quota or suspension, schema, recovery, durability, boundary encoding, lowering, machine representation, or family behavior, and it claims no performance, storage layout, or physical representation.

<a id="GNT-39.8-collection-value-model"></a>

**[GNT-39.8-collection-value-model] Collection value model.** This section publishes one value model for the admitted `Map<K, V>` and `Set<K>` constructed types of `GNT-39.4-map-type-form-recognition`: a `Map` value is its finite entries — each one admitted canonical key of `GNT-39.1-admitted-collection-keys` and the value that key resolves to — a `Set` value is its finite elements, each one admitted canonical key, because a set element is a collection key, and a `Range` value is its two bound positions over one admitted element type, ordered by `GNT-39.2-canonical-collection-order-and-duplicate-identity` with an inclusive start bound and an exclusive end bound, whose admissible step is exactly the sealed step contract of `GNT-39.7-range-step-contract`. A `Range` value whose start bound is not less than its end bound admits no position and no published rule refuses it, because both bound positions are values of the one admitted element type; its step is decided by the result-side rule of `GNT-39.7-range-step-contract` alone, and this clause composes no admission check into that bare step, so such a step can be reported for a source position the value does not admit, while the traversal next position publishes a position only for an admitted source. Admitting a value admits every candidate key under the key contract of `GNT-39.1-admitted-collection-keys`, refuses a repeated key under `collection-duplicate-key` before publishing anything, and publishes the admitted entries or elements in the canonical collection order of `GNT-39.2-canonical-collection-order-and-duplicate-identity`, so a value's observable content is exactly that ordered sequence and two values with equal entries are one value. A value's entries, elements, and bound positions are accounted as value nodes of the layer that carries the value: one `Map` entry is one node for its admitted key plus the nodes of the value that key resolves to, one `Set` element is one node, one bound position is one node, and the value itself is one aggregate node, so a carrying layer's node or nesting budget bounds exactly the content this clause publishes; content that exceeds that budget is refused by that layer's own resource-limit refusal rather than by any spelling of this section, which publishes no per-collection bound and no charge. This clause publishes the model and nothing more: it admits no source construction, source iteration protocol, mutation, ownership, invalidation, an exhaustion diagnostic, quota, suspension, schema, recovery, durability, boundary encoding, lowering, or physical machine representation. A collection value is carried by the canonical-IR contract as the value model itself — one value of the recognised `Map`, `Set`, or `Range` kind under the model that publishes it — and this clause admits no second representation and no physical layout claim; this edition admits no collection value as a member of a value-layer aggregate, so the accounting rule above applies exactly when a carrying layer admits one. A `Map` or `Set` value is never mutated in place: admitting one additional or replacement entry, or one element, publishes one new value in the canonical collection order of `GNT-39.2-canonical-collection-order-and-duplicate-identity`, an entry or element whose admitted content is unchanged publishes an equal value, the value it was published from is unchanged, and a cursor opened over that value keeps traversing exactly that value, so this clause publishes no in-place mutation and no invalidation rule. A carried value is traversable in its admitted content order: a `Map` value is traversed through its admitted entries and a `Set` value through its admitted elements, each visited exactly once in the canonical collection order of `GNT-39.2-canonical-collection-order-and-duplicate-identity`, and a visitor may end the traversal before the content is exhausted. A `Range` value is traversed stepwise: an admitted position is followed by the step the sealed contract of `GNT-39.7-range-step-contract` returns for it, a traversal that supplies no position begins at the inclusive start bound when that bound is present and admitted, an absent start bound publishes no first position, a position the value does not admit publishes no next position, and a pair that admits no position traverses to none. The visitor form reports no visit for a `Range` value, whose protocol is the stepwise one, so a caller dispatches on the carried kind before choosing a form. Traversal also publishes one temporary cursor form: a cursor borrows the value it traverses, each advance publishes the next visit or none at exhaustion, exhaustion being observed by an advance that publishes none rather than inferred from the value, and a `Range` cursor publishes positions through the same stepwise protocol the visitor form publishes no visit for. The cursor is exactly as long as the reference it holds, and because this clause publishes no mutation it publishes no invalidation rule, no ownership transfer, no source iteration protocol, no suspension, and no adapter over itself. Traversal also publishes one terminal fold form: a fold visits the same content in the same order with one accumulator, publishes the accumulator and how it ended, and consumes one step of the budget it is given per visit, so it always terminates and an unbounded `Range` side that publishes no end cannot make it run forever; reports `Stopped` with the accumulator it reached when the folder ends the fold or the budget is reached. Traversal also publishes one bounded view form: taking a budget publishes a view over the same content in the same order that publishes no more than that many visits, reports the advances it may yet spend, clearing them when an advance discovers the content is exhausted, holds its position rather than restarting, and publishes no visit at all at a budget of zero. Traversal also publishes one filtered view form: a filtered view advances over the same content in the same order, spends one step of the budget it is given per advance, publishes only a visit the predicate supplied to that advance admits, so a visit the predicate declines still spends its step and a later advance may supply a different predicate, publishes none once the budget is spent or the content is exhausted, and reports the visits it has published and the advances it may yet spend, clearing them when an advance discovers the content is exhausted. Traversal also publishes one enumerated view form: an enumerated view advances over the same content in the same order, spends one step of the budget it is given per advance, and publishes each visit with its zero-based position in that order, so the first advance publishes position zero, and it reports the visits it has published and the advances it may yet spend, clearing them when an advance discovers the content is exhausted. Traversal also publishes one paired view form: a paired view advances two values together, spends one step of the budget it is given per pair, publishes one visit from each value at the same zero-based position, ends when either value is exhausted so a visit already advanced from the longer value is published nowhere, and reports the pairs it has published and the advances it may yet spend, clearing them when an advance discovers that either value is exhausted. A remaining count of zero publishes no cause: it means the budget is spent or the content it advances is exhausted, and no form that publishes a remaining count reports which. Traversal also publishes one transformed view form: a transformed view advances over the same content in the same order, spends one step of the budget it is given per advance, publishes the value the transform supplied to that advance returns for the visit, and reports the visits it has transformed and the advances it may yet spend, clearing them when an advance discovers the content is exhausted. Traversal also publishes one collecting form: a collecting form advances over the same content in the same order, spends one step of the budget it is given per advance, projects each visit through the value the projection supplied to that advance returns, and publishes one list value of the canonical value contract holding those projections in that order together with how the traversal ended; the list is admitted under the value limits it is given once the traversal ends, so the projection runs for every advance that spends a step of the budget and content that exceeds those limits is refused by the value contract rather than by this clause. For every form of this clause that runs caller code, no transform, predicate, projection, or folder is invoked for an advance that discovers the content is exhausted. Traversal publishes no exhaustion diagnostic, and reports how a visitor-form traversal ended: `Completed` when every entry or element that form publishes was visited and `Stopped` when the visitor ended it early, while a `Range` value publishes no visit through that form and reports completion with none, its stepwise traversal reporting exhaustion by publishing no next position.
